h1: Whole-Home Surge Protection in Broward County
intro: South Florida throws more lightning and more grid switching at your home than almost anywhere in the country, and every spike travels your wiring looking for something with a circuit board in it. Whole-home surge protection installs at your panel and guards the entire system from one point. Our licensed crew checks the grounding it depends on first, then gives you one honest price for your property.

definition.heading: What whole-home surge protection does
definition.body: A surge protective device mounts at your electrical panel and stands between your home and voltage spikes, whether they arrive from the grid or start inside your own walls. Instead of protecting one device at a time the way a plug-in strip does, it guards every circuit in the house from a single point, before a surge ever reaches your outlets.

symptoms.title: A house full of sensitive electronics
symptoms.body: Televisions, computers, and appliances with circuit boards inside are easy for a single surge to take out at once. Protection at the panel guards all of it from one place.

symptoms.title: You are relying only on power strips
symptoms.body: Plug-in strips protect the one device plugged into them and wear out quietly over time. If they are your only defense, most of your home and its bigger equipment are unprotected.

symptoms.title: Appliances aging faster than they should
symptoms.body: Most surges start inside the home, small spikes every time a big motor like an air conditioner or pool pump cycles on. They rarely kill anything outright, but they wear down circuit boards year after year.

symptoms.title: Storm season keeps taking a toll
symptoms.body: A close strike or a grid switch after an outage can send a spike through the whole neighborhood at once. If storms have already cost you a television or an appliance, the next one does not have to.

process.title: The call and a few honest questions
process.body: You call and we talk through your property, what has failed before, and the equipment you most want protected.

process.title: The on-site assessment
process.body: We come out and look at your panel and your grounding, because protection at the panel is only as good as the ground it drains a surge into.

process.title: One honest price for the job that fits
process.body: We forecast the work and give you one price for protection matched to your panel and your property.

process.title: Our crew installs and closes it out
process.body: Our own licensed crew mounts the device at your panel and corrects the grounding if it needs it, and where the county requires a permit we pull it in our own name and meet the inspector.

benefits.title: One line of defense for the whole home
benefits.body: A panel-mounted protector guards your entire electrical system from a single point, before surges reach your outlets.

benefits.title: Covers surges from inside and out
benefits.body: It stands against grid spikes and lightning as well as the smaller surges your own equipment creates every day.

benefits.title: Installed on grounding we verified
benefits.body: A protector is only as good as the path it gives a surge to ground, so we confirm yours is sound before we call the job done.

benefits.title: Peace of mind before the next season
benefits.body: You stop dreading the forecast, knowing your electronics and appliances are guarded at the source.

localSections.heading: The lightning capital of the country
localSections.body: South Florida sits in the most lightning-prone corner of the United States, and every storm that rolls across Broward County in the summer pushes spikes onto the lines. Add the grid switching that follows outages and restorations, and homes here see far more surge events in a year than most of the country. Protection at the panel is not a luxury down here. It is the baseline.

localSections.heading: Older homes, corroded grounds, and problem panels
localSections.body: Broward County homes span many eras, and the grounding a surge protector depends on corrodes in salt air and humidity. On older homes we often find grounds that would not carry a surge safely, and problem-brand panels raise their own questions before anything new mounts to them. That is why we look at the whole picture in person before quoting, and leave a clean permitted record where one is required.

guide.title: The honest guide to surge protection in South Florida

sections.heading: Where surges actually come from
sections.body: Lightning and grid switching get the blame, and down here they earn it, but most surges start inside your own home. Every time a large motor cycles on, the air conditioner, the pool pump, the dryer, it sends a small spike back through your wiring. One spike does nothing you would notice. Thousands a year quietly shorten the life of every circuit board in the house, which is why appliances seem to age faster here.

sections.heading: Why the panel beats the power strip
sections.body: A plug-in strip protects a single device, wears out without telling you, and does nothing for the equipment you cannot plug into one, like the air conditioner, the range, or the pool equipment. A whole-home device mounts at the panel and clamps a surge before it spreads to your circuits. The two can work together as layers, but the panel is where real protection starts.

sections.heading: Grounding, honest limits, and choosing an installer
sections.body: A surge protector does not absorb a surge, it diverts it to ground, so it is only as good as the grounding under it, which we verify before we finish. Honest limits matter too: nothing sold for a home rides out a direct lightning strike to the roof. What protection at the panel does is handle the everyday spikes and the near misses that account for nearly all real-world damage. Choose a licensed installer who checks the grounding instead of just mounting a device and leaving.

faqs.question: What does whole-home surge protection actually protect?
faqs.answer: It guards your entire electrical system and everything tied into it, from televisions to appliances with circuit boards inside. Installed at the panel, it stands between your home and surges before they reach your outlets, unlike a plug-in strip that covers only one device. Many surges start inside your own home each time a large motor cycles on, and others arrive from the grid, so protection at the panel addresses the whole picture.

faqs.question: Will it protect my home from a direct lightning strike?
faqs.answer: We will be honest with you: no residential device rides out a direct strike to your roof, and anyone who promises that is overselling. What a panel-mounted protector handles is the far more common events, nearby strikes, grid switching, and the everyday spikes your own equipment creates. Those account for nearly all the surge damage homes actually see.

faqs.question: Do I still need it if I use good power strips?
faqs.answer: Strips are a fine second layer, but they only cover what plugs into them and they wear out without warning. Your air conditioner, range, pool equipment, and everything hardwired stays exposed. A panel-mounted device protects all of it from one point, and the strips then catch whatever little is left.

faqs.question: Do you install surge protection for commercial properties?
faqs.answer: Yes, for both homes and commercial properties across Broward County. A commercial building carries more sensitive equipment and often more to lose during downtime, and the same rule applies, the protection is only as good as the panel and grounding behind it. We assess the property in person and give you one honest price.
